note_text:
CC: Urinary urgency, frequency, and intermittent leakage x 6 months

HPI: 68-year-old woman presents with a 6-month history of urinary urgency, daytime frequency (voiding every 1-2 hours), and episodes of urge incontinence occurring several times weekly, requiring pad use. She denies dysuria, gross hematuria, or fever. She has failed a trial of behavioral modification (timed voiding, fluid management) and a 4-week trial of an anticholinergic (oxybutynin) without adequate symptom relief. She reports some sensation of incomplete emptying but no significant straining to void.

PMH: Hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus (well-controlled), no prior pelvic surgery.

Physical Exam: Abdomen soft, nontender, no palpable bladder distension. Pelvic exam reveals well-supported vaginal walls, no evidence of significant prolapse. Neurologic exam of lower extremities and perineal sensation intact, normal rectal tone.

Labs: Urinalysis with microscopy performed today in office: negative for leukocyte esterase, negative nitrites, no bacteria or WBCs seen on microscopy, no hematuria. Urine culture not indicated given clean urinalysis.

Assessment: Refractory overactive bladder with mixed features, failed conservative and first-line pharmacologic therapy. Given persistent symptoms despite treatment, and negative infectious workup, urodynamic evaluation is indicated to characterize detrusor function, assess for detrusor overactivity vs outlet obstruction, and guide decision-making regarding third-line therapy (sacral neuromodulation vs onabotulinumtoxinA).

Plan: Schedule multichannel urodynamic study (filling cystometry with pressure-flow voiding study) limited to the studies necessary to clarify the etiology of her voiding dysfunction — no additional testing beyond what is needed for this purpose. Will use findings to determine candidacy for third-line therapy. Continue current medications. Follow up after urodynamics to discuss results and next steps.
